var_desc: Variables and variable-level metadata capturing attitudes toward refugees/asylum seekers (single items and scales), related constructs (xenophobia, perceived threat, social distance, contact), and relevant sociodemographic controls.
var_narr: Include variable descriptions and codes for items asking about opinions on refugees (e.g., 'Do you support accepting refugees?', 'Would you accept a refugee as a neighbor?'), scales measuring xenophobia or refugee acceptance, and variables on contact, media consumption, political ideology, age, education and region used as covariates. Exclude variables that only record migration status of respondents without any attitudinal content or variables about migration flows/policies without linking to public opinion.

var_desc: Variable metadata for items and scales measuring general life satisfaction and related subjective well‑being indicators (item wording, response scales, scoring rules).
var_narr: Include variables representing single‑item life satisfaction measures (with response ranges), composite scores from validated scales (e.g., SWLS total score), indicators for affective well‑being if used alongside life satisfaction, and standard demographic covariates. Provide coding information, missing value handling, and scale reliability where available. Exclude variables limited to domain satisfaction only unless accompanied by a global life satisfaction variable.

var_desc: Variables and metadata for items and scales measuring general self‑efficacy (item text, response categories, total scores, reliability statistics).
var_narr: Include variable descriptions for each GSES item (or equivalent), computed total or mean scores for general self‑efficacy, reverse‑coding rules, and reliability (Cronbach’s alpha). Also include demographic covariates commonly used in analyses. Exclude variables that only reflect domain‑specific self‑efficacy constructs unless accompanied by a general self‑efficacy variable.

var_desc: Variables capturing antisemitic attitudes and behaviours: items on stereotypes, social distance, conspiracy beliefs, Holocaust denial, experiences of antisemitic incidents, and related demographic/contextual covariates.
var_narr: Include variable labels and item wording for antisemitism measures (e.g., agreement with antisemitic statements), coding for incident types, frequency counts, perpetrator/victim descriptors, and standard sociodemographic controls. Exclude variables that only measure general prejudice without items targeting antisemitic content.

var_desc: Variables describing employment and work: employment status, occupation, industry, working hours, contract type, wages, unemployment duration, job search and job quality indicators.
var_narr: Include variable metadata for standard labour market items (employed/unemployed/out of labour force), ISCO/ISCO-88/ISCO-08/ISCO-08 mappings, NACE industry codes, hourly/daily/weekly hours, contract permanence, earnings (gross/net), unemployment spells and reasons for job separation. Also include variables on training, commuting, multipart job holdings and workplace characteristics. Exclude variables unrelated to labour market outcomes (purely educational test scores) unless used to analyse employment.

var_desc: Variables capturing workload and occupational burden such as job demands, working hours, physical workload, psychosocial risk scales, absenteeism, and health outcomes related to work.
var_narr: Include variables measuring perceived workload, quantitative and qualitative job demands, time pressure, overtime, shift patterns, ergonomic strain, exposure to hazards, job control/decision latitude, effort-reward balance, burnout scales, stress, mental health symptoms, and sickness absence. Also include objective measures like recorded overtime hours, injury reports, and physiological stress markers if linked to work. Exclude generic stress variables with no linkage to occupational context.

var_desc: Variables representing global or facet-specific job satisfaction, affective and cognitive components of job attitudes, and related outcomes such as turnover intentions and organizational commitment.
var_narr: Include variables for overall job satisfaction, satisfaction with pay, promotion opportunities, supervision, colleagues, work tasks, working conditions, and work-life balance; also include job engagement, commitment, turnover intention, and intention to stay. Include both single-item satisfaction measures and validated multi-item scales. Exclude variables that measure only organizational outcomes without an employee-reported satisfaction component.

var_desc: Variables describing firm/establishment characteristics and workplace arrangements such as firm size, sector, ownership, management practices, collective bargaining, shift systems, and workplace safety policies.
var_narr: Include variables measuring establishment size, industry classification, ownership structure, presence of works councils or unions, HR practices (e.g. training, recruitment), shift organization, workplace safety measures, production technology, and employee composition by occupation. Include organizational outcome variables like productivity, absenteeism, and turnover at the firm level. Exclude variables that concern only individual attitudes without contextual linkage to the employing organization.

var_desc: Variables capturing work–life balance dimensions: work–family conflict/enrichment, flexible hours, telework, caregiving duties, commuting time, and perceptions of reconciliation between work and private life.
var_narr: Include measures of work-to-family and family-to-work conflict, work–life balance satisfaction, number of hours in paid and unpaid work, schedule flexibility, telecommuting frequency, childcare use, caregiving time, and uptake of family leave. Include outcomes like mental health, relationship quality, and job retention as they relate to work–life integration. Exclude variables unrelated to family or private life (purely occupational variables without linkage to non-work responsibilities).

var_desc: Core employment and work variables including employment status, occupation and industry codes, working hours, wages, contract type, job tenure, and measures of job quality and working conditions.
var_narr: Include variables for employment/unemployment status, full-/part-time, temporary vs. permanent contracts, occupation (ISCO), industry classification, hourly/weekly earnings, working hours, shift work, job tenure, training, and measures of job satisfaction and health as they relate to work. Also include standard demographic covariates used in labor research. Exclude variables that do not pertain to employment or the nature of work.

var_desc: Variables that measure aspects of occupational change and the evolving nature of work, including employment type, job tasks, skills and mobility indicators.
var_narr: Relevant variables: occupational codes and classifications over time (ISCO, national codes), job tenure, job-to-job mobility, incidence of temporary/atypical contracts, teleworking/remote work indicators, automation/technology-exposure measures, skill requirements/skill use scales, task content measures, part-time/full-time status, firm restructuring indicators. Exclude: variables that only measure generic demographics with no link to work change and variables limited to a single point in time without temporal comparability when the query concerns change.

var_desc: Variables that describe occupational status, job characteristics, career trajectories and vocational qualifications.
var_narr: Relevant variables: occupation codes (ISCO, KldB), industry sector, job title, employment status (employee/self-employed), occupational prestige and skill level measures, vocational qualifications/training indicators, career path indicators (promotions, lateral moves), job tenure, full-/part-time status, and wage linked to occupation. Exclude: variables unrelated to employment or that only record employer identifiers without occupational detail.

var_desc: Variables measuring job satisfaction, facets of satisfaction, and related predictors/outcomes (work conditions, pay, autonomy, health).
var_narr: Relevant variables: overall job satisfaction scores, facet-specific satisfaction (pay, supervision, tasks), Likert-scale items or validated composite scores (e.g. MSQ, JSS), variables on working conditions (hours, autonomy, demands), psychosocial risk factors, turnover intentions, absenteeism and mental/physical health indicators. Exclude: generic happiness variables without explicit reference to work, and variables that only capture employer-side satisfaction (management satisfaction with workforce) unless linked to employee outcomes.

var_desc: Variables capturing aspects of working conditions: physical demands, psychosocial factors, hours and scheduling, employment contract and safety exposures.
var_narr: Relevant variables: physical workload, ergonomic risk factors, exposure to hazards (noise, chemicals), psychosocial measures (demands, control, social support), working time (hours, shift/night work, overtime), contractual form (temporary, permanent, agency), occupational safety incidents, and workplace accommodations. Exclude: variables that only identify occupation without information on the conditions of work, or variables limited to non-work environmental exposures.

var_desc: Variables that define and measure unemployment status, duration, transitions, benefit receipt and job-search activities.
var_narr: Relevant variables: unemployment status (according to ILO definition), start and end dates of unemployment spells, duration of unemployment, prior employment history, receipt and type of unemployment benefits, job-search intensity and methods, reason for job loss, re-employment indicators, and demographic correlates (age, education). Exclude: variables that only measure inactivity without distinguishing unemployment (unless clearly coded), and economic indicators at aggregate level without microdata linkage when individual-level analysis is intended.

var_desc: Variables that capture aspects of commuting: commute time, distance, travel mode, number of transfers, departure/arrival times, cost, congestion measures, and subjective commute satisfaction or stress.
var_narr: Include measured or derived variables such as one-way travel time to work, round-trip commute duration, home–work distance, primary mode (car, public transport, bicycle, walking), multimodality indicators, peak/off-peak flags, route characteristics, commuting frequency, perceived commute stress, and exposures (air pollution, noise). Exclude variables that do not specify travel purpose or are aggregated mobility indices without work-specific attribution.

var_desc: Variables describing working time: weekly/annual hours, contractual vs actual hours, overtime, shift type, start/end times, irregularity, part-time/full-time status, and schedule control.
var_narr: Include numeric measures (paid hours per week/day, overtime hours), categorical indicators (shift work, night work, weekend work, flexible schedule), timing variables (typical start and end times), measures of schedule variability and predictability, and subjective items on satisfaction with working hours and perceived work–life balance. Exclude variables that only indicate employment status without any temporal detail.

var_desc: Variables indicating foreign or migrant status: country of birth, citizenship/nationality, migration background, year of arrival, residence permit type, language proficiency, and naturalization status.
var_narr: Include primary identifiers (country of birth, citizenship, nationality), derived measures (first/second generation, length of stay, age at arrival), legal status descriptors (refugee/asylum seeker, permanent/temporary permit), and integration-related measures (host-language skills, employment in host-country jobs). Exclude variables that only approximate migration indirectly (e.g., surname) unless linked to validated migration markers.

var_desc: Variables that quantify work-related burden: job demands, job control, effort-reward imbalance, physical load measures, exposure to hazards, perceived stress at work, and sickness absence related to work.
var_narr: Include validated scales and items (e.g., demand, control, support scores), numeric measures of physical workload (lifting weight, repetition rates), records of occupational injury, frequency/duration of sick leave, and subjective measures of burnout or exhaustion attributable to work. Exclude variables that capture generic psychological distress without attributing cause to work contexts.

var_desc: Variables capturing both work attributes and burden outcomes: job demands/control/support, physical exposures, work hours, plus stress, burnout, sickness absence, and performance metrics.
var_narr: Include paired variables such as measures of workload and corresponding stress/burnout scores, objective workload indicators (hours, caseload) with health outcomes (sick days, mental health diagnoses), and organizational performance indicators linked to employee burden. Exclude isolated variables that do not permit connecting work characteristics to burden outcomes.

var_desc: Variables measuring types and intensity of workplace burdens, associated health outcomes and work-related consequences.
var_narr: Include variables such as physical demands (lifting, repetitive movements), ergonomic risk scores, noise/chemical exposure levels, psychosocial demand/control/support scores, effort-reward imbalance, working hours/shift work, perceived workload, stress symptoms, burnout, musculoskeletal complaints, injury events, sick leave and absenteeism. Exclude generic mental health variables that lack linkage to workplace exposure or context unless usable as work-related outcomes.

var_desc: Core variables describing occupation, job classification and employment characteristics.
var_narr: Include variables such as job title, occupational code (ISCO/SOC), industry code, employment status (employed, unemployed, self-employed), contract type (permanent/temporary), working hours, occupational class, occupational prestige and sector. Exclude variables that do not refer to the job/occupation dimension.

var_desc: Variables capturing educational attainment, qualifications and their mapping to occupations and career outcomes.
var_narr: Include variables such as years of schooling, highest degree, ISCED/qualification codes, vocational certificates, field of study, training type, occupational code, job level, earnings, skill mismatch indicators and employment stability. Exclude generic academic performance measures that do not connect to occupational outcomes.

var_desc: Variables measuring overall and facet-specific job satisfaction, and related attitudes and outcomes.
var_narr: Include variables such as overall job satisfaction score, satisfaction with pay, tasks, supervision/co-workers, work-life balance, intrinsic/extrinsic satisfaction facets, turnover intention, organizational commitment and absenteeism. Exclude non-work-related well-being measures unless explicitly tied to occupational context.

var_desc: Variables capturing employment participation, job tasks, working time and occupational activity characteristics.
var_narr: Include variables such as employment status, hours worked, part-time/full-time indicator, primary job tasks, task complexity, occupational code, sector, employment spells, commuting and activity limitations at work. Exclude variables that only refer to non-work activities or general lifestyle measures.

var_desc: Variables that operationalize occupational mobility and career change: number/timing of job changes, change in occupational status, promotion/demotion indicators, tenure, sector change, occupational class codes, transition reasons and mobility matrices.
var_narr: Relevant variables measure job-to-job transitions (counts and dates), occupational codes before/after change (ISCO, national classifications), status/skill-level change (ISEI, EGP, prestige scores), promotion events, change in earnings, sector/industry change, geographic mobility for employment, employment status transitions (unemployed↔employed), and reasons for mobility. Exclude single-item variables only loosely related to mobility (e.g., current occupation only without prior history) or variables about organizational mobility of firms rather than individual career moves.

var_desc: Variables capturing work-related attitudes: work values (e.g., autonomy, security, income importance), job satisfaction scales, occupational aspirations, career intentions, and attitudes toward vocational training and employment policies.
var_narr: Relevant variables include Likert-scale items or indexes on importance of job attributes (security, income, status), measures of intrinsic/extrinsic work motivation, commitment to a profession, occupational aspirations and expectations, willingness to retrain, and evaluative items on vocational education. Exclude strictly behavioral variables (e.g., hours worked) or socio-demographic variables unless combined with direct attitude items.

var_desc: Variables operationalizing the 'professional self': occupational self-efficacy scores, identity centrality, identification with occupation/profession, perceived competence, vocational self-concept dimensions and stability of career identity.
var_narr: Include variables that measure confidence in performing occupational tasks, the importance of professional role to self-definition, statements of 'I see myself as a [profession]', measures of role conflict affecting professional identity, and scales for career commitment. Exclude generic self-esteem items unless explicitly framed in the occupational/professional domain.

var_desc: Variables capturing evaluation of social policy: support/opposition to welfare programs, satisfaction ratings, perceived fairness/effectiveness, willingness to pay/higher taxes for social programs, and trust in welfare institutions.
var_narr: Include Likert-scale or categorical measures of approval for specific social policies, overall satisfaction with the welfare state, perceived adequacy of benefits, perceived beneficiaries, and policy priority rankings. Also include variables on perceived redistribution preferences and willingness to finance policies. Exclude variables describing policy provision (eligibility, benefit amounts) unless paired with attitudinal assessments.

var_desc: Variables operationalizing the relationship with a supervisor: LMX scores, perceived supervisory support, trust in supervisor, frequency/quality of feedback, conflict/abuse indicators, and presence/quality of mentoring.
var_narr: Include validated measures such as LMX-7 items or composite scores, scales of perceived supervisor support, items on feedback frequency and developmental support, ratings of fairness and conflict with supervisor, and indicators of mentoring and sponsorship. Exclude generic management-level variables that do not capture the employee’s perception of their direct relationship with a supervisor.

var_desc: Variables capturing adult learning status and context: participation in courses, type of course, frequency/duration, modes (formal/non-formal/informal), motives, barriers, prior education, employment status, age, outcomes (skills, employment changes), and institutional affiliations.
var_narr: Include variables indicating adult education participation (binary/counts), course type and subject, hours spent in training, certification obtained, reasons for participation, obstacles to participation (cost, time, childcare), socioeconomic indicators (age, gender, education level, occupation), and measurable outcomes (literacy/numeracy scores, employment transitions, wage changes). Exclude variables strictly about school curricula, childhood learning milestones, or biomedical health measures unrelated to adult learning outcomes.

var_desc: Variables describing caregiving activity and context: caregiver status, hours of care provided, type of care tasks, paid/unpaid status, employment conditions, wages, training, relationship to care recipient, and care-recipient needs.
var_narr: Include variables indicating whether respondent is an informal or formal caregiver, weekly hours spent on caregiving, types of activities (personal care, medical assistance, household tasks), employment status and sector, contract type, wage level, access to training, extent of state support, care recipient characteristics (age, disability level), and measures of caregiver burden and wellbeing. Exclude variables that do not disaggregate care-specific activities or that only measure general household tasks without caregiving intent.

var_desc: Attitudinal variables: belief in anthropogenic climate change, perceived severity and risk, concern level, worry, perceived personal and societal impact, behavioral intentions, policy support, trust in science, and climate-related values and norms.
var_narr: Include variables measuring belief in climate change existence and causes (human vs natural), degree of concern or worry, perceived risk to self/community/nation, willingness to change behavior (e.g., reduce energy use, accept costs), support for specific policies (carbon tax, renewables, regulation), trust in scientific expertise, political ideology, and self-reported mitigation/adaptation actions. Exclude variables that only measure environmental attitudes in a generic sense without explicit mention of climate change.

var_desc: Physical and social variables relevant to climate research: atmospheric temperature, precipitation, greenhouse gas concentrations, emissions by sector, sea-level, extreme event counts, vulnerability indices, adaptation measures, mitigation policy indicators, and socio-economic covariates.
var_narr: Include variables capturing climate system metrics (mean/seasonal temperatures, anomalies, precipitation), emissions metrics (CO2, CH4 by source/sector), frequency/magnitude of extreme events, exposure and vulnerability measures (population at risk, infrastructure), policy variables (carbon pricing, renewable share), and socio-economic controls (GDP, demographics, land use). Exclude variables unrelated to climate processes or impacts (e.g., unrelated economic microdata without linkage to climate exposure).

var_desc: Variables reflecting conceptions and evaluations of democracy: support for democracy, preferred democratic attributes (participation, competition, rights), satisfaction with democracy, tolerance of non-democratic alternatives, perceived legitimacy, and related political attitudes.
var_narr: Include variables that ask respondents to define or choose what democracy means, rate importance of democratic elements (free elections, civil liberties, social justice), measure satisfaction with democratic performance, tolerance for authoritarian alternatives, trust in democratic institutions, and behavioral indicators like voting or protest participation tied to democratic beliefs. Exclude variables unrelated to conceptions (e.g., electoral results) unless used as contextual covariates.

var_desc: Variables measuring aspects of purchasing behavior, preferences, attitudes, and demographic correlates relevant to consumption.
var_narr: Include variables such as purchase frequency, spending/expenditure, product choice, brand awareness, willingness-to-pay, price sensitivity, purchase intention, satisfaction, loyalty, impulse buying, consumption occasions, and socio-demographics (age, income, household composition). Exclude firm financial indicators (profits, revenues) or macroeconomic aggregates that do not represent consumer-level behavior.

var_desc: Variables that capture infection status, clinical outcomes, preventive behaviors, and pandemic-relevant attitudes and exposures.
var_narr: Include variables such as SARS-CoV-2 test result, PCR/antigen status, symptom onset and severity, hospitalization, ICU admission, vaccination status and dose dates, compliance with NPIs (mask use, distancing), mobility indices, exposure history, serology results, and pandemic-related mental-health indicators. Exclude generic health variables that are not linked to COVID-19 without clear relevance.

var_desc: Variables capturing regime type, political participation, civil liberties, institutional arrangements, and democratic attitudes.
var_narr: Include variables such as regime classification (democracy/autocracy), electoral competitiveness, turnout, protest participation, trust in institutions, satisfaction with democracy, freedom of press indices, judicial independence, civil liberties scores, and party-system fragmentation. Exclude economic or social variables unless used to analyze their relationship with democratic outcomes and explicitly labeled as part of democracy research.

var_desc: Variables that quantify depressive severity, diagnosis, symptom profiles, treatment, and correlates.
var_narr: Include variables such as depression diagnosis (DSM/ICD), symptom scores (PHQ-9, BDI, CES-D scores), onset age, episode duration, remission status, suicide ideation/attempts, treatment type and adherence, comorbid anxiety, psychosocial stressors, and functional impairment. Exclude generic mood descriptors without validated measurement or clinical relevance.

var_desc: Variables describing access to, use of, skills with, and impacts of digital technologies.
var_narr: Include variables like internet access (broadband, mobile), frequency and type of online activities, digital literacy/digital skills scores, device ownership, platform engagement metrics, e-government service usage, teleworking frequency, and measures of digital inequality. Exclude variables that are unrelated to digital technology usage or that refer only to offline phenomena without a digital link.

var_desc: Variables capturing digital competence constructs and closely related indicators.
var_narr: Include variables that measure or proxy digital competence: objective test items/scores for digital tasks, composite competency indices, validated scale items (self-efficacy in digital tasks, digital problem solving), frequency of technology use for work/study, participation in digital training, familiarity with software/tools, and domain-specific digital skills (e.g. information evaluation, coding). Include sociodemographic variables and educational attainment as control variables when reported alongside competence measures. Exclude variables that only record device or network characteristics without behavioral or skill interpretation.

var_desc: Variables measuring digitalization at work, job tasks, automation risk and labor outcomes.
var_narr: Include variables capturing firm-level ICT adoption, presence of automation/AI, use of specific digital tools, frequency and intensity of digital task performance, job task descriptors, occupational task scores (e.g. routine vs non-routine), training in digital skills, telework incidence, contract type, wages, hours, employment status, job stability, productivity measures and health/wellbeing indicators related to digitalization. Also include industry, occupation codes, and demographic controls. Exclude variables only about consumer online behavior not tied to employment.

var_desc: Variables measuring digitalization processes and consequences at the workplace level.
var_narr: Include variables recording presence and type of workplace digital technologies (software, automation, collaboration tools), measures of task redesign, digital skill requirements, training provided, changes in work organization (remote work, flexible scheduling), productivity/performance metrics, absenteeism, occupational health outcomes, and employee perceptions of change. Include workplace identifiers, sector, size and management practices. Exclude variables that only indicate consumer device ownership or household internet access without workplace context.

var_desc: Variables reflecting digitalization exposure at job, worker and firm levels, and associated labor outcomes.
var_narr: Include measures of ICT use intensity, automation indicators, digital task frequency, required digital competencies, teleworking prevalence, platform work indicators, job insecurity, wages, productivity, and employment transitions. Also include occupational codes, industry identifiers and demographic controls. Include variables capturing training, upskilling and management responses. Exclude variables solely describing individual leisure internet use.

var_desc: Variables that measure discrimination, inequality and related constructs in school contexts.
var_narr: Include variables indicating student demographics (ethnicity, migration background, language status, socioeconomic status, disability status, gender, religion), indicators of school processes (tracking/streaming, streaming recommendations, special education placement), disciplinary records (suspensions, expulsions), teacher assessments/grades, test scores, measures of experienced discrimination or perceived bias, inclusion/exclusion indicators, and school-level composition and resources. Include variables capturing anti-discrimination measures or interventions. Exclude variables that cannot be disaggregated by group characteristics and therefore cannot inform discrimination analyses.

var_desc: Variable definitions and codebooks capturing measures of discrimination: self-reported experiences, perceived discrimination scales, victimization items, audit outcomes, complaint counts, and proxy indicators.
var_narr: Relevant variables are those explicitly measuring discrimination (e.g., 'experienced discrimination in last 12 months', 'ever treated unfairly because of ethnicity', perceived workplace discrimination scales), variables capturing discriminatory behaviors in experiments or audits (e.g., callback rates by applicant characteristic), and administrative indicators (complaints filed, decisions overturning discrimination claims). Exclude demographic variables that do not operationalize discriminatory experiences, and variables with ambiguous labels not tied to discrimination concepts.

var_desc: Variables relating to education: enrollment status, highest educational qualification, years of schooling, test scores, field of study, school characteristics, teacher-student ratios, and participation in educational programs.
var_narr: Relevant variables explicitly measuring educational dimensions: school attendance, grade repetition, qualifications attained, standardized test results, literacy/numeracy measures, type of school (public/private/vocational), classroom resources, teacher qualifications, and measures of educational attainment over time. Exclude variables that are tangential demographics with no clear educational meaning or ambiguous labels not tied to schooling or learning.

var_desc: Variables capturing attitudes toward Islam: feeling thermometers, agree/disagree items on Islam-related statements, perceived threat measures, policy preference items related to Muslim communities, and stereotype scales.
var_narr: Include variables explicitly assessing respondents' views about Islam or Muslims (e.g., 'warmth toward Muslims', 'Islam is compatible with democracy', 'are Muslims a threat to national culture'), measures of social distance from Muslims, and items on discriminatory preferences or policy support targeting Muslim populations. Exclude generic religiosity variables that do not specify attitudes toward Islam, or variables that only identify respondents' religion.

var_desc: Variables measuring attitudes toward immigration: support/opposition to immigration levels, policy preference items, perceived economic/cultural threat, openness to refugees, and social distance toward migrants.
var_narr: Include explicit attitude variables (e.g., 'allow more/fewer immigrants', 'immigrants are a threat to jobs/culture', 'would you accept immigrants as neighbors'), items on policy positions (border control, asylum), and scales measuring tolerance or prejudice toward migrants. Exclude variables that only identify migrants or immigrants as demographics without measuring respondents' attitudes.

var_desc: Variables that capture attitudes toward foreigners: feeling thermometers, social distance items, perceived threat scales, and policy preference questions specific to foreign populations.
var_narr: Include explicit variables such as 'warmth toward foreigners', 'would you accept foreigners as neighbors', 'foreigners take jobs from locals', support for restrictions on foreigners, and measures of xenophobic sentiments. Exclude general demographic variables indicating foreigner status or nationality that do not measure attitudes.

var_desc: Variable labels and operationalizations that capture attitudes toward foreigners/immigrants: social distance, xenophobia indices, acceptance scales, perceived threat, trust, and contact measures.
var_narr: Include variables named or operationalized as attitudes toward foreigners/immigrants, social distance (e.g., willingness to live next door/work with/marry a foreigner), xenophobia or prejudice scales, perceived economic/cultural threat, feeling thermometer scores for 'foreigners' or immigrant groups, and intergroup contact frequency/quality. Exclude demographic variables only (age, sex) unless they are combined with attitudinal measures, and variables that measure migration status alone without attitudinal content.

var_desc: Variables operationalizing attitudes toward gender: gender role ideology, support for equality, ambivalent sexism subscales, policy support, and stereotypes about male/female traits and capabilities.
var_narr: Include variables labeled or constructed as traditional/egalitarian gender attitudes, ambivalent sexism (hostile and benevolent sexism), beliefs about women’s employment or leadership, willingness to share domestic labor, and policy support for gender-equality measures. Also include variables measuring gendered stereotypes, perceived gender discrimination, and gender-targeted policy preferences. Exclude purely descriptive demographic variables or occupational classifications unless combined with explicit attitudinal indicators.

var_desc: Variables capturing attitudes to Islam/Muslims: favorability ratings, social distance items, perceived threat scales (cultural/security/economic), discrimination experiences, and policy preference variables.
var_narr: Include variables explicitly measuring views toward Islam or Muslims, such as feeling thermometer scores, willingness to accept Muslim neighbors/colleagues, indexes of Islamophobia, perceived compatibility of Islam with national values, and support/opposition to specific policies affecting Muslims. Also include variables for contact with Muslims and media exposure to Islamic issues. Exclude general religiosity measures that do not specify attitudes toward Islam or Muslims.

var_desc: Variables describing employment outcomes in Poland: employment/unemployment status, sector/industry, occupation codes, contract type, working hours, wages/salary, job tenure, and labor market transitions.
var_narr: Include variables indicating current employment status (employed, unemployed, inactive), detailed occupation (ISCO), industry (NACE), full-/part-time status, temporary/permanent contract, net/gross wages, hours worked, job search activity, and reason for job exit/hire. Also include variables on informal employment and cross-border commuting when relevant to Poland. Exclude variables unrelated to labor (e.g., clinical health measures) unless linked to employment outcomes.

var_desc: Variables operationalizing dimensions of work alienation: powerlessness, meaninglessness, normlessness, isolation, self-estrangement, lack of autonomy, and low task significance.
var_narr: Include variables explicitly labeled as alienation or constructed from items addressing feelings of powerlessness at work, lack of control/autonomy, work being meaningless or monotonous, social isolation from colleagues, inability to realize oneself in work, and related indices combining these facets. Also include related measures such as job satisfaction, organizational commitment, and burnout when used to assess alienation. Exclude purely economic variables (wages/hours) unless combined with subjective alienation measures.

var_desc: Variables operationalizing environmental conditions, exposures, perceptions, attitudes and behaviours, e.g., pollution indices, green space proximity, ecological indicators, and measures of environmental concern or pro-environmental behaviour.
var_narr: Relevant variables include objective environmental measures (PM2.5, NOx, water contaminants, biodiversity indices), GIS-derived measures (distance to parks, land-cover percentages), and socio-psychological variables (environmental concern, risk perception, frequency of recycling, energy consumption, willingness-to-pay). Exclude variables that only incidentally mention 'environment' without measuring environmental attributes or attitudes (for example, a variable labeled "environment" that is a general control for context with no environmental meaning).

var_desc: Variables capturing environmental attitudes and related constructs: scale scores (NEP, environmental concern indices), single-item measures (concern about climate change), and related belief/perception indicators.
var_narr: Relevant variables are composite scores and individual items assessing environmental concern, ecological worldview, perceived seriousness of environmental problems, climate change belief, support for environmental policies, and self-reported pro-environmental behaviours. Include coding information, item wording, response scales and psychometric properties. Exclude variables labeled ambiguously that do not measure attitudes (e.g., purely behavioural or objective environmental metrics) unless paired with attitudinal items.

var_desc: Variables measuring aspects of Erziehung: parental practices, disciplinary strategies, educational activities, home learning environment, teacher attitudes, and child development outcomes.
var_narr: Include variables capturing parenting styles (authoritative, authoritarian, permissive), frequency of parent–child activities, disciplinary measures, indicators of early learning environment (e.g., HOME inventory items), school pedagogy variables, and child cognitive and socio-emotional outcome measures. Exclude variables unrelated to upbringing or educational socialization (e.g., purely economic indicators) unless directly used to study Erziehung.

var_desc: Variables used in social work evaluation: client outcomes (well-being, employment, recidivism), service usage, fidelity indicators, process measures, and contextual factors affecting program success.
var_narr: Relevant variables include standardized outcome scales (quality of life, symptom scales), indicators of service access and intensity, recidivism or re-referral rates, client satisfaction, and implementation/process measures (caseworker contacts, adherence to protocol). Include socio-demographic covariates commonly used in evaluation. Exclude variables that do not inform intervention effectiveness or implementation (e.g., unrelated administrative codes) unless necessary for record linkage.

var_desc: Variables operationalizing external political efficacy and closely related constructs: survey items and composite indices measuring perceived responsiveness of government, influence over political decisions, and trust in institutions.
var_narr: Include individual items (e.g., 'People like me have no say in what the government does'), composite external efficacy scales, and coding information (item wording, response categories, scoring). Also include related variables such as political trust, internal political efficacy, political participation, and socio-demographics used as covariates. Exclude poorly defined variables that do not capture perceptions of institutional responsiveness.

var_desc: Key variables on family composition and employment: parental employment status, working hours, occupation, job tenure, leave usage, childcare arrangements, number/age of children, marital status, and household income.
var_narr: Include variables that measure: current employment (employed/unemployed/out of labour force), working hours (hours/week, part‑time/full‑time), occupation/industry, job contract type, career breaks, maternity/paternity/parental leave (duration, uptake), childcare use and costs, number and ages of children, household composition, partner's employment, household income, education, commute time, and job flexibility. Also include subjective measures: perceived work–family conflict, job satisfaction related to family, and employer support. Exclude variables unrelated to family or employment (e.g., detailed clinical biomarkers) or variables without documentation for coding.

var_desc: Variables capturing career and family events: promotion history, earnings, job tenure, job mobility, occupational status, leave spells, number/age of children, and partner employment.
var_narr: Include variables measuring career outcomes (wages/income, promotions, occupational status/authority level, full/part‑time status, job tenure and contract type, career interruptions, re‑entry timing), and family indicators (date of childbirth, number/age of children, caregiving responsibilities, spousal employment). Also include education, training participation, workplace policies available, and subjective career aspirations. Exclude variables that do not allow linking family events and career timelines.

var_desc: Measures of gender attitudes, division of household labour, time spent on childcare/domestic tasks, employment by gender, parental leave uptake by gender, and household decision‑making indicators.
var_narr: Include variables such as: responses to gender attitude statements (e.g., views on working mothers, male breadwinner model), time‑use minutes by activity and by household member, caregiver role indicators (primary carer), distribution of specific chores, parental leave uptake and duration by sex, employment status by gender, negotiation/decision‑making variables, and indicators of childcare arrangements. Also include demographic controls (age, education, cohort). Exclude generic demographic variables without gendered household context.

var_desc: Core family variables: household composition, marital/cohabitation status, number and age of children, parental status, kin availability, household income, fertility histories, residential arrangements, and intergenerational transfers.
var_narr: Include variables that allow characterization of family structure and dynamics: household roster entries, relationship to head, marital status, partnership dates, childbirth dates, fertility histories, number/age of children, coresidence with parents/children, caregiving receipt/provision, household income and resources, housing arrangements, and measures of family support and conflict. Also include demographic controls (age, sex, education, region). Exclude variables that cannot be linked to family units or lack sufficient metadata.

var_desc: Variables linking gender and family: sex/gender of household members, gender attitudes, time spent on domestic and care work by gender, parental leave uptake by sex, employment status by sex, and measures of intra‑household decision making.
var_narr: Include variables that permit analysis of gendered family dynamics: respondent sex/gender, partner's sex/gender, gender identity if available, allocation of household chores and childcare by gender, paid/unpaid work hours by gender, parental leave and flexible work uptake by sex, attitudes toward gender roles, measures of power/decision making in the household, and indicators of gendered outcomes (income gaps, career interruptions). Also include intersectional markers (education, ethnicity). Exclude variables without gender or family relevance.

var_desc: Variables that operationalize the concept of employment form: employment_status, contract_type, job_type, employment_relation, working_hours, hourly_hours_category, part_time_indicator, temporary_contract_indicator, self_employed_flag, tenure_months, multiple_jobs_flag, gig_worker_flag, telework_indicator, agency_worker_flag.
var_narr: Relevant variables: fields explicitly capturing type of employment contract/arrangement (permanent vs. temporary; full- vs. part-time; self-employed vs. employee), working hours and schedule, source of contract (agency/platform), number of jobs, and measures of contract precarity (duration, notice period). Prefer variables with standardized coding (ILO/EU definitions) or clear codebooks. Exclude variables that only indicate employer legal form or occupational classification without any contract/arrangement information.

var_desc: Variables that capture leader-related trust and related constructs: trust_in_leader, trust_in_management, perceived_leader_integrity, perceived_leader_competence, leader_member_exchange_score (LMX), organizational_trust, interpersonal_trust_at_work.
var_narr: Relevant variables: items or composite scores that explicitly reference trust toward supervisors/management or measure dimensions of trust (affective vs. cognitive), perceived leader fairness/honesty/competence, LMX indices, and measures of team-level trust. Prefer variables with validated German translations. Exclude generic societal trust variables that lack explicit workplace or leader referents unless used as contextual comparison.

var_desc: Variables operationalizing leadership: leadership_style, transformational_leadership_score, transactional_leadership_score, authoritarian_leadership_flag, leader_effectiveness_rating, leadership_self_efficacy, LMX_score, leadership_experience_years.
var_narr: Relevant variables: measures that capture leaders' behaviors, styles and effectiveness (self, subordinate or peer ratings), leader characteristics (tenure, role), and follower outcomes attributed to leadership. Prefer validated composite scores (e.g., MLQ subscales, LMX). Exclude variables that vaguely reference managerial position without any measure of leadership behavior or influence.

var_desc: Variables representing gender-role attitudes and role behavior: gender_role_attitudes, traditional_gender_role_index, egalitarianism_score, attitudes_toward_women_working, childcare_responsibility_belief, division_of_household_labor, bem_sex_role_inventory_scores.
var_narr: Relevant variables: items or scale scores that explicitly measure normative beliefs about gendered responsibilities (housework, childcare, breadwinner role), self-reported role behaviors, and identity-based role measures. Prefer validated scales (AWS, BSRI) and harmonized items across waves. Exclude variables that only indicate respondent sex/gender with no attitudinal or behavioral content.

var_desc: Variables capturing gender constructs: gender_identity, sex_at_birth, current_gender, gender_expression, gender_nonconformity_flag, gender_role_attitudes, reported_discrimination_due_to_gender, gender_binary_flag.
var_narr: Relevant variables: explicit measures of gender identity (including non-binary/transgender options), variables distinguishing sex and gender, measures of gender norms and experiences (discrimination, roles), and harmonized codes for analysis. Prefer clearly documented coding and, for identity measures, inclusion of open/other categories. Exclude variables that only indicate biological sex when the intended concept is social gender identity or norms.

var_desc: Variables capturing gender identity, gender roles and norms, attitudes toward gender equality, gendered behaviours, and intersectional attributes linked to gender.
var_narr: Include: variables named gender, sex assigned at birth, gender identity, gender expression, masculinity/femininity scores, gender role attitudes, division of household labour, childcare responsibility, experiences of discrimination by gender, intersectional identifiers (race, class, sexuality) that interact with gender. Exclude: physiological or clinical biomarkers used solely for biological sex classification where no social/gender interpretation is provided.

var_desc: Variables representing general self‑efficacy, usually operationalized as scale total scores or subscale scores from validated instruments.
var_narr: Include: variables labeled general self‑efficacy, GSE_total, self‑efficacy_score, aggregated Likert scale scores from general self‑efficacy instruments, and item‑level variables for psychometric analysis. Exclude: variables that measure only situational or task‑specific self‑efficacy unless accompanied by a general self‑efficacy measure.

var_desc: Variables enabling identification or characterization of Generation Y and their characteristics: birth year, age, cohort indicators and common outcomes studied for this group.
var_narr: Include: birth_year, age_at_survey, generation_label (e.g., 'Millennial', 'Generation Y'), employment status, educational attainment, family formation markers, technology usage, political attitudes and other variables frequently analyzed by cohort. Exclude: variables that cannot be linked to respondent age or birth cohort.

var_desc: Variables measuring general self‑efficacy in German datasets: scale totals, item responses, and variable labels such as 'generelle_Selbstwirksamkeit' or 'SWE'.
var_narr: Include: variables for Gesamtscore der Allgemeinen Selbstwirksamkeit, individual item variables (Likert responses), and related constructs (self‑confidence, coping expectations) when linked to the general self‑efficacy concept. Exclude: variables referring solely to situational Selbstwirksamkeit without a general measure.

var_desc: Variables that operationalize gender roles and related attitudes/behaviours: role attitude scales, time use in domestic tasks, occupational sector by gender, and masculinity/femininity measures.
var_narr: Include: variables such as gender_role_attitude, household_task_hours, childcare_responsibility, Bem masculinity/femininity scores, attitudes toward women's employment, and indicators of occupational gender composition. Exclude: simple sex or gender identifiers without accompanying role or attitude measures.

var_desc: Variables that operationalize gender role concepts: attitudinal items, behavioral indicators, role allocations, and demographic covariates.
var_narr: Include variables measuring gender role attitudes (agreement with statements about expected male/female behaviors), self-reported division of household labor and care, occupational role and employment status by gender, role conflict/role strain scales, measures of gender identity related to roles, and relevant demographics (sex, age, education, marital status). Exclude variables that only record sex/gender without any role-related content, and variables unrelated to social roles (e.g. purely biological measures).

var_desc: Variables reflecting collective and individual-level gender role norms: stereotype endorsement, expectations for men/women, distribution of household tasks, occupational segregation indicators.
var_narr: Include variables such as agreement with stereotypical statements, reported primary caregiver/household responsibilities, indicators of occupational concentration by gender, measures of normative pressure, and community- or country-level aggregates of role attitudes. Exclude isolated biological health markers or administrative codes that do not inform about roles or norms.

var_desc: Variables commonly used in health research: morbidity, mortality, diagnoses, self-rated health, health behaviors, biomarkers, utilization and socioeconomic determinants.
var_narr: Include variables such as ICD/diagnosis codes, self-rated health, chronic condition indicators, prevalence/incidence measures, BMI, blood pressure, smoking/alcohol use, physical activity, health service use (visits, hospitalizations), and socioeconomic covariates. Exclude variables unrelated to health outcomes or determinants.

var_desc: Variables measuring psychiatric diagnoses, symptom severity, psychological well-being, suicidality, treatment and service use, and mental-health-relevant covariates.
var_narr: Include variables such as ICD/DSM diagnoses, scores on PHQ-9, GAD-7, GHQ-12, BDI, WHO-5, psychiatric hospitalization, medication use for mental disorders, measures of stress and resilience, and functional impairment. Exclude variables that do not concern mental health (e.g. general biomarkers without linkage to mental health).

var_desc: Variables pertaining to patient status, clinical diagnoses, treatment modalities, outcomes, service use, and patient-reported measures.
var_narr: Include variables like diagnosis codes, treatment type, medication, length of stay, readmission, mortality, clinical outcome measures, PROMs, patient satisfaction, adherence, comorbidities, and socio-demographics of patient groups. Exclude variables unrelated to patient care or outcomes (e.g. organizational finances) and variables from non-patient samples.

var_desc: Variables measuring workplace health management, organizational exposures, and aggregated employee health outcomes.
var_narr: Relevant variables include company-level indicators (presence of health promotion programs, occupational safety policies, number of occupational health staff), aggregated sickness absence rates, work-related injury rates, workplace exposure metrics (noise, chemicals, ergonomics), measures of psychosocial work environment at organizational level (e.g., job demands, control, support), and indicators of program implementation and reach. Exclude variables that measure only individual clinical biomarkers unrelated to work context or demographic-only variables without workplace linkage.

var_desc: Variables capturing individual and contextual measures of health and working conditions within the workplace.
var_narr: Include individual health outcomes among employees (self-rated health, musculoskeletal complaints, mental health symptoms, sickness absence), workplace exposure variables (physical, chemical, ergonomic, psychosocial), job characteristics (occupation, shift work, working hours), and organizational factors (management practices, safety climate). Exclude variables that do not connect health measures to employment or workplace context.

var_desc: Individual health indicators and employment-related variables relevant to the health of workers.
var_narr: Relevant variables encompass self-rated health, diagnosed conditions, mental health scales (depression, anxiety), musculoskeletal complaints, frequency and duration of sickness absence, presenteeism measures, workplace exposures, job characteristics, occupational class, and health behaviors among employees. Exclude variables that solely measure organizational attributes without linking to employee health outcomes.

var_desc: Variables that capture self-reported symptoms, somatic complaints, and psychosomatic indicators.
var_narr: Include variables for frequency, severity, and duration of specific complaints (musculoskeletal pain, headaches, fatigue, sleep disturbances, gastrointestinal complaints), composite symptom scores, psychosomatic symptom scales, and health-related quality-of-life items tied to complaints. Include variables that record timing and work-related attribution of complaints. Exclude laboratory-only biomarkers that do not reflect patient-reported symptoms.

var_desc: Variables measuring types, frequency, severity, timing, context, and consequences of violent acts and exposures.
var_narr: Relevant variables include indicators of physical assault, sexual violence, intimate partner violence, child abuse, workplace violence, bullying, hate-motivated incidents, exposure to political/collective violence, PTSD and other health sequelae, injuries resulting from violence, perpetrator relationship, and reporting and service utilization. Include variables on protective factors and prevention exposure. Exclude variables unrelated to violent behavior or exposure.

var_desc: Variables that measure youth-directed or youth-perpetrated violence and related outcomes (victimization, perpetration, frequency, severity, context, and correlates).
var_narr: Include variables such as self-reported victimization (physical, sexual, emotional), bullying victim/perpetrator indicators, dating violence measures, exposure to domestic violence, number of incidents, severity indicators, location/context of incidents (school, home, online), perpetrator relationship, help-seeking, reporting to authorities, protective factors (e.g., parent supervision), and mental/behavioral health outcomes linked to violence. Exclude variables that are generic criminal counts without age attribution or that measure only non-violent behaviors (unless explicitly linked to violent acts).

var_desc: Variables that operationalize life satisfaction and global subjective well‑being, including single-item and multi-item scales and country-level aggregates.
var_narr: Include variables for global life satisfaction such as Cantril Self-Anchoring Scale (ladder), single-question life satisfaction items (e.g., 'All things considered, how satisfied are you with your life?'), Satisfaction With Life Scale (SWLS) scores, country-level average life satisfaction indicators, and demographic moderators (age, gender, income, education). Also include variables capturing domain satisfactions contributing to life satisfaction (health, income, social support). Exclude variables that measure only momentary affect without evaluative life satisfaction or purely domain-specific outcomes unlinked to overall life evaluation.

var_desc: Health-related variables capturing status, behaviors, outcomes, determinants, and service use (e.g., self-rated health, chronic conditions, BMI, mental health scores, healthcare utilization).
var_narr: Include self-rated health measures, diagnosed chronic condition indicators, morbidity and mortality measures, biomarkers (e.g., blood pressure, cholesterol) when linked to population data, mental health screening scores (PHQ-9, GHQ), health behaviors (smoking, alcohol, physical activity), BMI, functional limitations, health insurance status, healthcare utilization metrics, and socioeconomic determinants of health. Exclude purely administrative coding subsets without health-relevant fields or variables only about laboratory assays without linkage to population health outcomes.

var_desc: Variables capturing remote work arrangements and outcomes: telework frequency/intensity, work hours/location, job satisfaction, productivity, work–family conflict, and home workspace characteristics.
var_narr: Include variables indicating whether respondents work from home, number of days/hours worked at home, employer telework policy, availability of equipment, self-reported productivity, job satisfaction, stress and mental health measures linked to remote work, commuting time saved, work–life balance measures, ergonomic conditions of home workspace, and household composition while teleworking. Exclude variables that only indicate general internet use without relation to work or those that track purely leisure activities at home.

var_desc: Variables that identify and characterize migrants and migration processes: country of birth, citizenship, migration reason/status, length of residence, legal status, language proficiency, and integration outcomes.
var_narr: Include variables such as migrant status (immigrant, emigrant, refugee, asylum-seeker), country of birth, citizenship, parental country of birth, year of arrival, length of stay, legal residency status, reason for migration, language skills, education credentials, employment and income, housing, naturalization, social integration indicators, and access to services. Also include remittance behavior and transnational ties when linked to migration. Exclude variables that do not permit identification of migration-related attributes or that only measure temporary travel for tourism.

var_desc: Variables that measure or are commonly used to analyze inequality: income, wages, wealth, consumption/expenditure, occupational status, education level, health indicators, household composition, region, race/ethnicity, gender, and derived inequality indices (Gini, Theil).
var_narr: Include variables capturing individual or household economic resources, demographic attributes, labor market outcomes, educational attainment, health measures, and geographic identifiers that allow subgroup comparisons and inequality decomposition. Also include derived variables and indices explicitly labeled as inequality measures. Exclude variables that do not permit assessment of disparities (single-case identifiers without demographic/contextual attributes) or highly aggregated indicators that prevent subgroup or distributional analysis.

var_desc: Variables assessing trust in information and sources: trust scales for media/institutions/experts, perceived credibility ratings, source trustworthiness, exposure to misinformation, fact-checking behavior, and confidence in knowledge.
var_narr: Include validated items and indices measuring trust in specific information sources (e.g., television news, online news, social media), general media trust, perceived accuracy/credibility of messages, willingness to share, and behavioral proxies (clicks, shares tied to trust judgments). Exclude variables that measure unrelated forms of trust (e.g., generalized social trust) unless they are explicitly linked to information contexts.

var_desc: Variables capturing aspects of information policy and politics: legal/regulatory indicators, transparency scores, censorship flags, frequency of information control events, access-to-information metrics, and measures of government communication practices.
var_narr: Include variables that operationalize policy environments (presence/strength of data protection laws, FOI provisions), measures of censorship or content takedowns, indices of media freedom, counts of state information campaigns, and measures of public access to government information. Exclude purely technical variables describing system performance (latency, throughput) unless linked to political/policy outcomes (e.g., digital infrastructure affecting access to information).

var_desc: Variables measuring ICT-related phenomena: internet access, device ownership, connection type and speed, frequency and purposes of use, digital skills, online activities (social media, e-commerce, e-government), and barriers to access.
var_narr: Include variables that record household/individual-level ICT access (broadband, mobile), skills assessments, online engagement measures, location-based infrastructure indicators, and socioeconomic covariates enabling analysis of the digital divide. Exclude technical-only metrics (packet loss, port numbers) that do not inform social research on ICT adoption or effects.

var_desc: Variables measuring political interest and attentiveness: self-reported interest in politics, frequency of following news/politics, attention to public affairs, political discussion frequency, and indices of political engagement.
var_narr: Include single-item and multi-item measures where respondents report their level of interest in politics, how often they follow political news, and related behaviors (discussing politics, civic participation). Also include derived scales combining related items. Exclude variables that only measure political knowledge tests without attitudinal indicators unless paired with explicit interest measures.

var_desc: Variables that operationalize interest in leadership: leadership aspiration, desire to be a manager, willingness to lead, promotion intent, leadership career intentions, and related constructs (leadership motivation).
var_narr: Include single-item and multi-item scales that explicitly ask about wanting to lead, seeking managerial positions, or choosing leadership responsibilities. Include demographic moderators (age, gender, tenure) when paired with leadership interest variables. Exclude variables that only measure leadership behaviors, efficacy, or style without assessing interest/aspiration.

var_desc: Variables measuring work motivation and related constructs: intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, work engagement, motivation regulation, goals at work, task significance, autonomy, and motivational outcomes (effort, persistence, turnover intention).
var_narr: Include validated scales (e.g., UWES, Work Extrinsic and Intrinsic Motivation Scale) and survey items that explicitly assess motivational orientation or intensity at work. Include job characteristics known to affect motivation (autonomy, task variety) when linked to motivation measures. Exclude variables that only capture general attitudes toward work without assessing motivational constructs.

var_desc: Variables that quantify job satisfaction: overall job satisfaction scores, facet scales (pay, supervision, coworkers, work itself), single-item satisfaction indicators, and related wellbeing measures tied to job satisfaction.
var_narr: Include both global and domain-specific job satisfaction variables and their subscales. Include demographic and occupational covariates when analyzed in relation to job satisfaction. Exclude variables that only measure job performance or engagement if job satisfaction is not included.

var_desc: Variables relevant to adolescents: age-specific indicators (grade, pubertal stage), education status, mental health measures (depression, anxiety), risk behaviors (substance use, delinquency), family background, peer relations, and transition markers (vocational training, school-to-work).
var_narr: Include variables that directly measure adolescent experiences, developmental status, health and behavior. Include validated measures used with youth (e.g., SDQ). Exclude adult-only measures or variables not applicable to adolescent contexts (e.g., retirement status).

var_desc: Variables pertinent to children and adolescents: developmental milestones, cognitive and socio-emotional measures, physical health indicators, vaccination and growth data, schooling and attainment, child welfare indicators, and family socioeconomic variables.
var_narr: Include variables valid for child and adolescent assessment (e.g., CBCL, developmental screening scores, school performance, family structure). Include age-appropriate health and behavior measures. Exclude adult-only indicators (employment status for older adults, retirement) and measures not applicable to minors.

var_desc: Variables that measure climatic conditions, drivers, impacts, and public responses: temperature, precipitation, humidity, CO2/CH4 concentrations, sea level, extreme event indices, vulnerability indicators, adaptation measures, climate risk perceptions.
var_narr: Relevant variables include quantitative meteorological measures (daily/monthly/annual temperature, precipitation, drought indices), greenhouse gas concentrations, derived indices (heatwaves, cold spells, extreme precipitation), and socio-economic variables tied to climate impacts (crop yield losses, health outcomes). Also include attitudinal variables about climate concern and policy support. Exclude variables that use 'climate' only as a metaphor (e.g., corporate climate) unless clearly environmental.

var_desc: Variables that capture change and responses: trends in temperature and extreme events, emission rates, radiative forcing, vulnerability/adaptation indicators, mitigation behaviors, belief in anthropogenic climate change, policy support measures.
var_narr: Relevant variables measure temporal changes (e.g., decadal temperature trend), frequency/intensity of extremes, CO2 emissions per capita, indicators of adaptive capacity, and attitudinal measures about climate change causes and policy preferences. Exclude static environmental descriptors that do not relate to change unless used to assess change or vulnerability.

var_desc: Variables capturing cultural aspects: participation frequencies, cultural capital indicators, language use, ethnic and cultural identity, values and norms measures, attendance at cultural events, funding/support levels for arts and heritage.
var_narr: Relevant variables include measures of cultural participation (visits per year), self-reported cultural identity, proficiency/use of languages, indicators of cultural capital (education, tastes), attitudes toward cultural diversity, and institutional measures (number of cultural organizations, funding amounts). Exclude laboratory culture measures and variables unrelated to social/cultural phenomena.

var_desc: Variables measuring workplace learning: participation in training (type, duration), informal learning activities, mentoring received, skill acquisition measures, training costs, employer support, learning outcomes (skill tests, wages, promotion), and workplace learning culture indicators.
var_narr: Relevant variables capture occurrence and intensity of on-the-job training, certification achieved, frequency of informal learning, employer-provided training hours, individual learning strategies, and outcomes such as productivity or career progression. Exclude variables that measure non-learning aspects of work unless used to analyze learning processes (e.g., job tenure only used to study learning opportunities).

var_desc: Variables that operationalize left-right orientation: self-placement on left-right scales, composite ideological scores (economic/social dimensions), party identification mapped to left-right, issue-based scales aggregated into left-right orientation, and extremes/moderation indicators.
var_narr: Relevant variables include 0–10 or 1–7 left-right self-placement items, factor scores from issue items representing left-right dimension, categorical left/center/right labels, and consistency measures between self-placement and policy attitudes. Exclude variables measuring non-ideological left/right concepts (body orientation, handedness).

var_desc: Variables that measure media exposure, consumption, content, engagement, trust, source credibility, platform use, frequency, duration, and media effects (attitudes, knowledge, behavior).
var_narr: Include variable names and descriptions that capture types of media used (TV, radio, print, online, social media platforms), frequency and duration of media use, intensity of engagement (likes, shares, comments), content categories (news, entertainment, political content), trust in media, perceived bias, source credibility, exposure to specific messages or campaigns, and measures of media effects (knowledge change, attitude change, behavioral intentions). Exclude variables that use the word 'media' in non-communication senses (e.g., culture media in labs) or variables that are too generic without a clear relation to media use or content (e.g., a variable named 'channel' without context).

var_desc: Variables describing job characteristics such as autonomy, task complexity, workload, hours, contract type, physical demands, psychosocial risks, role clarity, and training requirements.
var_narr: Relevant variables explicitly measure attributes of work: job autonomy/control, decision latitude, task variety, repetitiveness, physical workload, exposure to hazards, psychosocial stressors (job demands, social support), working time arrangements (shift work, part-time), contract permanence, overemployment/underemployment, training/skill requirements, and indices of job quality. Include variables coded at worker or job level. Exclude variables that only indicate employment/unemployment status without detailing work characteristics.

var_desc: Variables capturing migration status and characteristics: country/region of birth and residence, migration history, legal status, reason for migration, duration, language proficiency, integration indicators, remittances, and mobility patterns.
var_narr: Relevant variables include migrant origin and destination, date/year of migration, duration of stay, citizenship and legal/permit status, refugee/asylum status, reason for migration (economic, family, conflict), return intentions, language skills, employment status and occupational mobility, social integration measures, remittance sending/receiving, and household composition changes because of migration. Exclude variables named 'migration' that refer to cell or animal movement in biological studies.

var_desc: Variables describing employees: demographic and employment attributes, job tenure, contract type, wages, performance measures, satisfaction, absenteeism, turnover intentions, training participation, and workplace relations.
var_narr: Relevant variables explicitly measure characteristics of employees: employee ID, age, gender, education, occupation, tenure, contract type (permanent/temporary), salary/wage, working hours, job grade, promotion history, performance ratings, job satisfaction, organizational commitment, intention to leave, absenteeism, participation in training, and supervisory relationships. Exclude variables where 'mitarbeiter' appears as an author or contributor label but not as an employee characteristic.

var_desc: Variables measuring mobility: travel frequency, trip distance and duration, mode of transport, commuting time, origin and destination, mobility constraints, accessibility indices, and indicators of social/mobile career mobility.
var_narr: Relevant variables include number of trips, trip purpose, mode choice (car, bike, public transport, walking), travel time and distance, frequency of travel, commuting patterns, car ownership, access to transport, mobility limitations, accessibility scores, intergenerational occupation/income mobility measures, and modal shift indicators. Exclude variables that use 'mobility' in purely biological or physical senses unrelated to human movement or social mobility unless clearly contextualized.

var_desc: Variables capturing employee motivation and related workplace constructs (intrinsic/extrinsic motivation, engagement, satisfaction, commitment, turnover intention).
var_narr: Include variables representing validated motivational constructs (e.g., intrinsic/extrinsic motivation scores, work engagement subscales, job satisfaction indices, organizational commitment, motivation-related predictors like leadership style, rewards, autonomy) and key covariates (role, tenure, occupation, industry). Exclude variables unrelated to workplace motivation (e.g., general cognitive tests) unless explicitly analyzed as predictors of employee motivation.

var_desc: Variables representing motivation in learning contexts: intrinsic/extrinsic motivation, goal orientation, task value, self-regulation, and learning outcomes.
var_narr: Include variables such as intrinsic/extrinsic motivation scores, achievement goals, task value, self-efficacy for learning, study strategies, persistence, time on task, course completion, and assessment scores. Include demographic and contextual covariates (age, educational level, instructional format). Exclude variables unrelated to learning motivation (e.g., general workplace engagement) unless linked to training/learning outcomes.

var_desc: Variables capturing personal and situational interest and related motivational constructs (engagement, persistence, value, curiosity).
var_narr: Include variables for personal interest, situational interest, curiosity, task value, intrinsic/extrinsic motivation, engagement, time on task, and persistence. Include contextual moderators (topic domain, learning environment). Exclude unrelated variables (e.g., financial interest metrics) unless clearly operationalized as psychological interest.

var_desc: Variables describing media use behavior: frequency, duration, platform type, device, purpose, multitasking, and media content categories.
var_narr: Include variables such as daily/weekly hours spent on specific media, number of sessions, platform identifiers (TV, radio, social media, streaming services), device used, purposes (news, social contact, entertainment), measures of multitasking, and related demographic covariates. Exclude variables that refer only to technical content delivery parameters (bandwidth, packet loss) unless tied to user consumption patterns.

var_desc: Variables capturing online sport participation and outcomes: usage frequency, session duration, physical activity metrics, performance stats, adherence, and engagement indicators.
var_narr: Include variables such as number of online workouts, minutes of activity per session, step counts/heart rate from wearables during online sessions, e-sports performance indicators (scores, rankings), attendance of live classes, user engagement measures (comments, likes), and self-reported fitness outcomes. Include demographics and device/platform identifiers. Exclude variables that do not differentiate online from offline sport activity.

var_desc: Variables capturing vocational interests, occupational intentions, career decision-making, guidance received and transition outcomes.
var_narr: Relevant variables measure career aspiration, preferred occupation, RIASEC codes or interest inventories, vocational guidance attendance, counseling outcomes, career decision self-efficacy, perceived fit, reasons for occupational choice, apprenticeship enrollment, time to employment after education. Include variables coded for analysis (scales, indices, categorical occupational choices). Exclude generic employment variables with no information on orientation or preferences, and variables referring to other kinds of 'orientation' (e.g., geographic orientation).

var_desc: Variables operationalizing personality traits, facets, temperament, and related scales or indices.
var_narr: Include variables representing Big Five domains and facets, personality disorder scales where applicable, temperament dimensions, composite personality indices, item-level responses for personality questionnaires, and reliability/scale information. Include coding for reverse-scored items and normative tables if available. Exclude variables that do not measure personality (e.g., single impressions or interviewer assessments that are not validated personality measures) or broad demographic descriptors mislabeled as 'personality.'

var_desc: Variables capturing types and frequencies of political participation, intensity, and forms of civic engagement.
var_narr: Relevant variables include voter turnout, intention to vote, protest attendance, petition signing, contacting public officials, party/campaign volunteering, political donations, membership in political organizations, frequency of civic actions, and composite participation indices. Include variables that distinguish conventional vs. unconventional and offline vs. online participation. Exclude generic social participation variables without a political dimension (e.g., sports club membership) unless explicitly coded as political/civic.

var_desc: Variables measuring internal/external political efficacy, perceptions of political influence and institutional responsiveness.
var_narr: Include variables for internal efficacy (e.g., 'I consider myself well-qualified to participate in politics'), external efficacy (e.g., 'People like me have no say in what the government does'), composite efficacy indices, item-level responses, and coding for directionality and scale. Include information on reverse-coded items and reliability. Exclude variables measuring general self-efficacy, efficacy in non-political domains, or attitudinal items not interpretable as efficacy.
